exposure: History of vaginal bleeding prior to onset of labor
Presence of fever prior to admission
outcome: Admission to the Neonatal Special Care Unit
cohort: 392 women with preterm labor between 24 to 28 weeks of gestation and their newborns at Kawempe National Referral hospital in Kampala, Uganda
finding: Caesarean delivery was associated with lower perinatal mortality, maternal infections, postpartum hemorrhage, and admission to the Special Care Unit compared to vaginal delivery in preterm deliveries between 24 to 28 weeks of gestation.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery is the preferred mode of delivery for preterm deliveries between 24 to 28 weeks of gestation, especially when labor is not established in low-resource settings, as it is associated with fewer adverse pregnancy outcomes compared to vaginal delivery.
